results.comment: I'm sitting here crying because I've spent my entire self-conscious life struggling with the negative (and more often than not, accurate) stereotypes associated with men where I self-excluded from my own social and sexual needs from fear of being a "monster". If I bring this up, or talk about the loneliness, or inability to connect, I get told to shut up because somehow the privileges that I received against my will from a society I had no part in building overshadow the harrowing suffering I've dealt with since I was 8. I'm studying to be a psychologist, and the ratio boys/girls is easily 1:40; and this is a massive issue for a profession that relies so fundamentally on cognitive empathy, which is ever so sensitive to biases and especially gender biases, even more so when the representations about health on the other side of the gender frontier are so heavily informed by mediatization of certain issues. Reading all of these comments resonates hard with me and I'm thankful to have found this video. I'm not sure I agree that starting boys a year later is the way to go because that would just lead to SFP. Boys are less advanced > rob them of a year's worth of education > boys are less advanced. The whole education system is honestly a huge steaming pile of shit and that is true everywhere in the world except the big outliers so it's no wonder we can't "suggestion" away issues related to inequality in an already maladaptive system though. It's not a system made for subjectivity and human creativity; it's made for analytical skill and industrial productivity. Still, going to try to snatch the book. Happy trails folks!

results.comment: 1:55 here in Brazil we also have a 14% gap (57%-43%). Despite free university education many men struggle to pursue it, largely bc they are often expected to work from a young age, sometimes as early as 15 to help support their families. It's rly common to see 15yr boys working to contribute financially to their families, while their 20yr sisters are not held to the same expectation and stays in their home studying. And, upon finishing high school at 18, men face mandatory military service here in brazil, which delays/disrupts their educational progression. With many men working from an early age, they simply lack the time to dedicate themselves to studying as intensely as women can. Often, young women can focus solely on academics until they are like 22 or even 25, without any responsibility, spending all day preparing for university entrance without the same economic pressures. results.comment: This video is amazing, its truly articulate, and I greatly appreciate that!  There are not enough women in this comment section, so here I am. I think that this subject is very touchy and that's why there aren't so many women here. Though my initial reaction was dismissal I decided to watch the video. I think there are certainly some valid points stated, especially because I see the education gap in my own experience. In a class of 30 there are two boys in my AP Literature class. In my AP Calculus class, there's likely more boys than girls, but maybe it's a 17:13 or so; it's not particularly drastic. While some part of me, the prideful part likely, wants to argue that there's still inequality in society for women—and there is—I also think that we do need to listen to men too. However, I think it's important to distinguish, we need to listen to men, when men are talking about men, or the human race as a whole. We need to listen to men when they're talking about wanting more support, but not when they talk of bringing women down, because I've seen the latter far too often recently. It can't be argued that NO men want women's inequality back, but it would also be unfair to say all men want that. I feel, and maybe this is just me, but I feel that we need to provide more support systems for men in areas where they are drastically unsupported. We need to do so without bringing down those supports for women. Finally, we need to change our attitudes because what causes inequality is fear of inequality the other way.  Sorry for the essay. Just my thoughts. If you disagree that's fine, but please do so respectfully; I am young and have a lot to learn, but berating is by no means teaching. Thank you for consideration.
results.comment_focus_summary: The commenter is reflecting on gender representation and inequality in education and society, arguing for listening to men on some issues while supporting women and creating support systems for men without reducing women's gains.
